# SplitButton

Header: `winui/ui/input/SplitButton.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/input/SplitButton.hpp`.

A button with a second, chevron part that opens a flyout.

The primary part raises [on_click()](#on_click) and runs the command; the 35 DIP secondary part at the right (or Alt+Down / F4) opens the flyout below the button. As for every flyout anchor, the flyout owns the split button: make it the flyout's anchor and the flyout wires itself in through [set_flyout()](#set_flyout). The declarative form is [ui::SplitButton](#uisplitbutton), usually as a [ui::Flyout](flyout.md#uiflyout)'s `.anchor`.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<ui::Color> current{ui::colors::Black};
ui::Property<ui::Color> ink{ui::colors::Black};

window.set_content(ui::Flyout{
    .anchor  = ui::SplitButton{ .text     = "Choose color",
                                .on_click = [&] { ink = current.get(); } },
    .content = ui::HorizontalStack{ .spacing = 4, .content = {
        ui::Button{ .text = "Red",  .on_click = [&] { current = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFFFF0000); } },
        ui::Button{ .text = "Blue", .on_click = [&] { current = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF0000FF); } },
    }},
});

// Imperatively:
auto  flyout = std::make_unique<ui::FlyoutControl>();
auto* split  = flyout->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::SplitButtonControl>("Choose color"));
flyout->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Pick a color"));
split->on_click([&] { ink = current.get(); });
```

## `ui::SplitButton`

A button with a second part that opens a flyout. Builds a [ui::SplitButtonControl](#uisplitbuttoncontrol).

The primary part raises [`.on_click`](#uisplitbutton-on_click) and runs [`.command`](#uisplitbutton-command); the secondary part (the chevron) opens the flyout the split button is the `.anchor` of, below it and left-aligned.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::string> current{"Red"};
ui::Property<std::string> ink{"Black"};

window.set_content(ui::Flyout{
    .anchor  = ui::SplitButton{.text     = "Choose color",
                               .on_click = [&] { ink = current.get(); }},
    .content = ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
        ui::Button{.text = "Red", .on_click = [&] { current = "Red"; }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Blue", .on_click = [&] { current = "Blue"; }},
    }},
});
```

```cpp
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control,
    .content
}
```

## `ui::ToggleSplitButton`

A split button whose primary part also toggles [`checked`](#uitogglesplitbutton-checked). Builds a [ui::ToggleSplitButtonControl](#class-togglesplitbuttoncontrol).

The chevron opens the flyout it is the `.anchor` of, as [ui::SplitButton](#uisplitbutton)'s does. [`.checked`](#uitogglesplitbutton-checked) is two-way with a [`Property<bool>`](../core/property.md) or a [`Property<std::optional<bool>>`](../core/property.md): the button shows the property and a click on the primary part writes it back, before [`.on_checked_changed`](#uitogglesplitbutton-on_checked_changed) runs.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> bullets{false};

window.set_content(ui::MenuFlyout{
    .items   = {{.text = "Bullets"}, {.text = "Numbers"}},
    .anchor  = ui::ToggleSplitButton{
        .text                  = "List",
        .checked               = bullets,
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::ToggleSplitButton{
    .text, .checked, .padding, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .enabled, .accessibility, .command, .command_parameter, .on_click, .on_checked_changed,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

### automation_providers

```cpp
void automation_providers(AutomationProviders& out) override
```

Lists what a client can do with this node: set `out`'s field for each pattern this control implements now to `this`, through the provider interface it inherits privately (ui/Automation.hpp). A pattern that only applies in some states is an `if`. `out` arrives empty, and nothing is listed by default.

Example: 
```cpp
class Chip final : public ui::Element, private ui::InvokeProvider
{
protected:
    void automation_providers(ui::AutomationProviders& out) override
    {
        out.invoke = this;
    }

private:
    bool invoke() override
    {
        on_click_();
        return true;
    }
    ui::Callback<void()> on_click_;
};
```

## class ToggleSplitButtonControl

Derives from `ui::SplitButtonControl`, `ui::ToggleProvider`.

A [SplitButton](#uisplitbutton) whose primary part also toggles [checked()](#checked). Checked, both parts draw in the accent colors. The declarative form is [ui::ToggleSplitButton](#uitogglesplitbutton).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> bullets{false};
ui::Property<int>  bullet_style{0};

window.set_content(ui::Flyout{
    .anchor  = ui::ToggleSplitButton{ .text    = "Bullets",
                                      .checked = bullets }, // two-way
    .content = ui::VerticalStack{ .content = {
        ui::Button{ .text = "Round", .on_click = [&] { bullet_style = 0; } },
        ui::Button{ .text = "Square", .on_click = [&] { bullet_style = 1; } },
    }},
});
```

## Enumerations

### SplitButtonState

```cpp
enum class SplitButtonState
```

The visual state a [SplitButton](#uisplitbutton) draws in. A checked [ToggleSplitButton](#uitogglesplitbutton) draws the same states in the accent colors.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Normal` | At rest. |
| `Disabled` | is_enabled() is false. |
| `FlyoutOpen` | The flyout is open: both parts drawn pressed. |
| `TouchPressed` | Space or Enter held: both parts pressed. |
| `PrimaryPointerOver` | The pointer is over the primary part. |
| `PrimaryPressed` | The primary part is pressed. |
| `SecondaryPointerOver` | The pointer is over the chevron part. |
| `SecondaryPressed` | The chevron part is pressed. |
